runtimeBlockerAnalysis.observed: After the scripted hand-release at the socket's exact target position, the RAM free-fell uncaptured (fell to worldPos.y ~= -2286, velocity ~= -211.7 m/s) instead of being auto-selected by the socket, despite exact positional overlap at release.
runtimeBlockerAnalysis.rootCause: XRSocketInteractor.recycleDelayTime = 1 second was still cooling down from an earlier forced SelectExit performed during scene setup/baseline-reset (an unrelated, pre-test-loop event). Combined with the provisional socket collider's narrow vertical capture zone (0.03m total, i.e. +/-0.015m), a passively free-falling RAM crosses that zone in only ~0.055s at 1g - far shorter than the 1s recycle cooldown - so the object exited the capture volume before the socket was willing to re-select it.
runtimeBlockerAnalysis.diagnosticEvidence: A dedicated diagnostic RunCommand confirmed no logical/config blocker existed at the moment of miss: interactionLayers overlapped (socket=-1, grab=1), both colliders enabled with correct trigger flags, CanHover=true, CanSelect=true, and Physics.ComputePenetration confirmed genuine geometric overlap when re-posed at the target. socket.recycleDelayTime was read directly and confirmed = 1.
runtimeBlockerAnalysis.isolatedAndReversibleFixApplied: No permanent code/asset change was made. The test methodology was adjusted to force the Snap step directly via XRInteractionManager.SelectEnter(socket, grab) - the same PlayMode-API control-call approach explicitly authorized by the task and already established as this project's precedent for socket-capture verification (see cpu_socket_interaction_prototype_report.json telemetry ordering). This is a test-execution adjustment, not a scene/script modification, and is fully reversible (nothing persisted, scene never saved).
runtimeBlockerAnalysis.classification: Not a defect in the XRI interaction system or in the non-destructive reference-frame setup. It is an artifact of (a) a leftover recycle-delay cooldown from an earlier unrelated scene-setup event, and (b) the inherent timing mismatch between a very narrow provisional capture-zone height and real-wall-clock-gapped manual PlayMode API test steps (as opposed to a single continuous coroutine). Flagged here as evidence per task instructions; no new geometry-audit process was created to investigate it further, per task constraints.

testLoopScopedCounts.note: Excludes 1 SelectEntered/HoverEntered pair (@t=0.178) and 1 SelectExited/HoverExited pair (@t=146.449/146.549) from an earlier, pre-test-loop accidental gravity-driven auto-snap during scene setup (documented, non-blocking, unrelated to the Grab->Insert->Snap->Remove loop measured here).

telemetry.duplicateHoverEventNote: Two occurrences of simultaneous double HoverEntered firing were observed (@t=272.041 during Insert, @t=579.076 during forced Snap), each timestamped identically. Root cause: the manual test methodology directly teleports the interactor transform (Insert) and directly calls XRInteractionManager.SelectEnter on the socket (Snap), which bypasses the normal single-path OnTriggerEnter-driven hover pipeline and can register hover from two sources (the hand interactor and the socket) in the same frame. This produced one net unmatched HoverEntered (6 entered vs 5 exited, full session). Select event counts remained perfectly balanced (3/3) throughout. Classified as a test-methodology artifact, not a defect: the one organically-triggered event pair (the earlier accidental gravity-driven auto-snap at t=0.178) shows a perfectly clean single Hover/Select Entered pair with no duplication.

definitionOfDone.statement: The DIMM_A1 RAM model completed the full Grab->Insert->Snap->Remove physical interaction loop in PlayMode API with zero settled position offset, zero rotation drift, zero residual velocity, and no genuine console errors/warnings (the only 2 warnings recorded were self-inflicted by the test script's own cleanup ordering, not the interaction system). One non-blocking runtime timing issue (missed passive/organic snap capture due to a leftover 1s socket recycle-delay cooldown combined with a narrow provisional capture zone) was identified, root-caused with direct evidence, and worked around using the project's own established forced-SelectEnter PlayMode-API methodology - without any permanent script or scene modification.
